explanation: Processor pipelining improves instruction execution speed by overlapping the execution stages of multiple instructions.  Forwarding is a crucial technique within pipelined architectures that addresses data hazards. Data hazards occur when an instruction needs data that hasn't yet been produced by a previous instruction in the pipeline. Forwarding mechanisms provide the necessary data directly from intermediate pipeline stages to avoid stalls, ensuring efficient pipelined execution.
syntax: Forwarding logic is implemented as a complex set of conditional statements determining the data source based on pipeline stage and destination/source register dependencies.  Priority is given to the latest available value of a register from the earliest possible pipeline stage.
example_explanation: This Y86-64 code demonstrates a data hazard. The first two `irmovq` instructions write to register %rdx. The `rrmovq` instruction reads from %rdx.  Without forwarding, the `rrmovq` would read an outdated value of %rdx from the register file. Forwarding ensures `rrmovq` gets the latest value (3) from the execute stage, instead of the older value (10) still present in the memory stage, accurately simulating sequential execution.
